text: Historical Cycle is a category of Irish myth. Irish texts often divide myths into four cycles. These are the Mythological Cycle, the Ulster Cycle, the Fenian Cycle, and the Historical Cycle. The Historical Cycle holds stories that may have happened between late Celtic and early Christian times, roughly the third through the eleventh century. Many tales rest on real events. Myths and supernatural happenings embellish them. The stories often turn on Tara, the important ritual and political center. They also concern Sovereignty, the Celtic concept of right rulership. Kings in the Historical Cycle include Conn of the Hundred Battles, Cormac Mac Airt, Mongan, and Guaire.
